🚨🇲🇽 MEXICO DECLINES RUBIO'S SUMMIT TO BRAND THE LEFT AS "TERRORISTS"

Marco Rubio invited some 60 countries to a July 16 Washington summit against what he calls "transnational extreme-left terrorism." Mexico said no. Sheinbaum's government declined the invitation outright — Mexico and Brazil were singled out for special invites as the region's two largest left-led economies, precisely the governments a summit like this exists to target. Mexico won't lend its name to it.

🇲🇽✊ Money straight to the schools — no middlemen. "In 2026, 22.69 billion pesos go directly to 71,482 schools across the country." — Pamela López Ruiz, director of La Escuela es Nuestra, July 13 The program hands resources directly to school committees of parents and teachers, who set their own priorities. Under Sheinbaum it expanded to secondary and high schools, reaching 100% coverage there for 2025-2026, with primary and preschool targeted for 2027.

🇲🇽🏭 Mexican sugar wins back its US export quota. "The US is raising its import quota for Mexican sugar. This is excellent news." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, July 13 Mexico recovered its sugar export quota to the US market for this cycle and the next. Sugar is a strategic rural industry — thousands of cane-growing families depend on the export, and the restored quota brings certainty to the country’s mills.

🇲🇽🔍 Sheinbaum distances her government from the CNDH’s Ayotzinapa report. "We did not participate in any way in that report. That has to be very clear." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, July 13 The National Human Rights Commission (CNDH), an autonomous body, issued a recommendation on the Ayotzinapa case. Sheinbaum said her government had no role in it and instructed the Interior Ministry to review it thoroughly. The investigation into the 43 disappeared students continues.

🇲🇽🏭 Inflation fell to 3.37% — the lowest since 2020. "General inflation stood at 3.37% in June 2026, the lowest since December 2020, falling for a third straight month." — César Escalante, head of consumer agency Profeco, July 13 The PACIC basic-goods basket held steady at 910 pesos. Tomatoes fell 39%, poblano peppers 40%, alongside drops in eggs and limes. 80% of gas stations are honoring the sub-27-peso diesel price agreement.

🇲🇽✊ A record 59 billion pesos for public schools this year. "A historic investment of 59 billion pesos for the country’s schools." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, July 13 Education Secretary Mario Delgado detailed 58.4 billion pesos in infrastructure for 2026: 37.7B for basic education, 10.9B for high schools (31 new campuses, 370 new national prep schools), and 9.8B for universities targeting 330,000 new spots. Over 22 million students will receive scholarships this year.

🚨🇲🇽 "Every party, without exception." "I call on Congress and every political party, without exception, to demand information too. This is a matter for all Mexicans." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, July 13 Sheinbaum framed the defense of nationals killed in ICE custody as a national cause above partisanship — moving from diplomatic notes to formal criminal complaints in US courts and demanding an impartial investigation.

🚨🇲🇽 Mexico is taking the deaths of its citizens in ICE hands to US courts. "We have to raise our voice when the human rights of our people are violated. We can't keep sending diplomatic letters that have produced no results." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, July 13 Seventeen Mexicans have died in ICE custody or operations — 14 in detention centers, 3 during raids, including Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, shot by ICE agents in Houston on July 7. On July 13 Mexico’s Foreign Ministry filed criminal and civil complaints with the US Department of Justice and state prosecutors.
